expected_answer: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a framework that combines document retrieval with a sequence generation model to produce more accurate and knowledge-grounded answers.
The RAG architecture consists of a neural retriever that fetches relevant documents and a sequence generator that produces the final answer using the retrieved information.
A dense vector index enables efficient semantic retrieval of documents that are relevant to the input query.
The retriever searches the indexed knowledge base and returns the most relevant documents for the query.
The generator produces the final response by conditioning on both the user query and the retrieved documents.
RAG reduces hallucinations by grounding the generated response in retrieved external knowledge instead of relying only on the model's parameters.
Parametric memory refers to knowledge stored in the model weights, while non-parametric memory refers to external documents retrieved at inference time.
Retrieved documents provide factual context that guides the generator toward producing accurate and grounded answers.
Knowledge-intensive tasks require access to large amounts of factual information, which RAG can retrieve dynamically from an external knowledge source.
Compared with a standard language model, RAG can access up-to-date external knowledge, improve factual accuracy, and provide more grounded responses.
